unifyFloor.reason: user-reported defect: every rock edge had a pale lacy band and every pool a dark crosshatch band, because each corner tile's own floor-region pixels are independently generated by the AI alongside its upper terrain, so they never quite match the canonical floor tile's grain -- reads as a halo once the sheet is tiled.
unifyFloor.tool: scripts/tiles/postprocess.py's unifyfloor subcommand/unify_floor() function -- already added by a sibling agent (crystal biome) by the time this agent first checked, per the dispatch's re-check instruction, so it was reused rather than re-implemented from scratch.
unifyFloor.problem found: unify_floor's colour-only classification, run at its own default tolerance (9), incorrectly replaced ~58% of the SOLID rock tile (storedMask 15, no floor corners at all) with floor pixels -- fungal's pale bracket-fungus crust sits close enough to the dark-loam floor's palette in Lab space that colour distance alone isn't a reliable discriminator for this biome's overlapping muddy palette.
unifyFloor.fix: originally patched around with a one-off wrapper (.sandbox/tiles-biomes/unify_geo.py) that post-filtered unify_floor's output by a bilinear corner-geometry 'floor-ness' weight. Per a later housekeeping request, this was upstreamed into the shared tool itself as an OPT-IN `corner_mask`/`mask_bit`/`min_floor_weight` parameter set on `unify_floor()` (and matching `--corner-mask`/`--mask-bit`/`--min-floor-weight` CLI flags on the `unifyfloor` subcommand) -- see scripts/tiles/postprocess.py's `_corner_floor_weight()` helper and the `unify_floor` docstring. Omitting `--corner-mask` reproduces the exact prior behaviour (verified byte-identical for callers that don't pass it, e.g. crystal/bone/flooded/volcanic's existing usage); passing it intersects the geometric weight (>= `--min-floor-weight`) with the colour classification BEFORE the morphology cleanup pass, so a tile with zero floor corners is provably untouched regardless of colour overlap. A `selftest` case (solid-upper tile, full colour overlap with the floor palette, `corner_mask=0`) covers this in the shared script.
unifyFloor.command: python3 scripts/tiles/postprocess.py unifyfloor <graded_tile_i.png> --floor-ref art/tiles/fungal/work/graded_v2/floor_ref.png --corner-mask <i> --mask-bit lower --min-floor-weight 0.3 --tolerance 9 <out.png> (run once per tile 0-14 for rock, 0-15 for water, <i> = the tile's own PixelLab file index, which IS a valid --corner-mask value directly in the 'lower' convention)
unifyFloor.verifiedResult: solid rock tile (corner_mask=0, no floor corners): 0/576 px changed (was 336/576 at colour-distance-only, pre-guard). Partial tiles (masks 3/5/7/10/12 sampled): 74-210/576 px replaced, visibly smoothing the floor-side grain without eating into the fungal rock/spore-pool silhouette. Confirmed in the room mockup: no pale/dark banding around the 2x2 pillar block, the lone pillar, or the water pool edges.
unifyFloor.appliedTo: rock_v2 tiles 0-14 and water_v2 tiles 0-15 (rock tile_15 is the floor reference itself, skipped) -- applied AFTER grading, so the floor reference it unifies against is already at the target darkness/chroma
unifyFloor.upstreamRebuild: rock_v2 and water_v2 were regenerated end-to-end through the shared `unify_floor()` call (same params as the wrapper) and diffed pixel-for-pixel against the wrapper-produced tiles already packed. water: all 16 tiles byte-identical. rock: 8 of 16 tiles (masks 1,4,5,8,9,10,11,12) differ by 2-5 px out of 576 each (<1%) -- all isolated boundary pixels a few px from the floor/upper transition edge, a consequence of the shared implementation intersecting the geometry mask with the colour mask BEFORE the small-hole/speck morphology pass, vs the wrapper's coarser post-hoc revert-after-morphology approach. No structural difference (no missing chunks/holes), confirmed by eye in a full pixel-value dump of every differing pixel. The shared-command output was adopted as the new canonical source and repacked; the wrapper (.sandbox/tiles-biomes/unify_geo.py) is no longer used.
